mainTopic: The five grains: their source for חלה and מצה, how grain forms join together, and the timing of חדש and the עומר
overview: The גמרא finishes naming the five grains and infers that rice and millet are not obligated in חלה. ריש לקיש learns this from a גזרה שוה on the word לחם, which links חלה to מצה. מצה itself must come from grain that can become חמץ, and rice and millet only rot. Next, a ברייתא says grain, flour and dough join together, and the אמוראים argue about which law this is for: חדש, חמץ on פסח, מעשר שני, or, according to רבא, food impurity, where only plain food joins. A ברייתא about shelled and unshelled barley supports רבא, and the גמרא settles a contradiction by splitting moist grain from dry grain. The גמרא then gives sources for why חדש and the ban on reaping before the עומר apply only to the five grains. רבי יונה and רבי יוסי בר זבדא argue whether 'before the עומר' means before its reaping or before its offering. The משנה's wording leads the גמרא to move their argument to the clause about grain that took root before the עומר. רבי אלעזר then begins a response that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Naming the grains in everyday language
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes giving the everyday names for the grains in the משנה: כוסמין is גולבא, שיפון is דישרא, and שיבולת שועל is שובלי תעלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: [כוסמין is] גולבא; שיפון is דישרא; שיבולת שועל is שובלי תעלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is translating the grain names from the משנה into the Aramaic names people used in daily life, so we know exactly which plants are meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list started just before this line. The first word, גולבא, finishes the sentence that identifies כוסמין. The point is practical: the law only works if we can recognize these plants in the field.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the five grains (often called spelt); here called גּוּלְבָּא
One of the five grains (often called rye); here called דִּישְׁרָא
One of the five grains (often called oats); literally 'fox's ear of grain'

phrases.english: [spelt is] gulva;
shifon is dishra;
shibbolet shual is shubbolei ta'ala.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the identification of the משנה's grains that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's grain names match the everyday Aramaic names גולבא, דישרא and שובלי תעלא.

steps.title: Only these grains, not rice or millet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the list: these five grains are obligated in חלה, but rice and millet are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: These, yes. Rice and millet, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a short conclusion from the list: only the five grains count, and rice (אורז) and millet (דוחן) are left out. This sets up the next question, which asks for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rice and millet look like grains and can be made into a kind of bread, so you might think they count. The גמרא says they don't, and that claim needs proof. That is the question it asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These, yes': these are included
Rice
Millet

phrases.english: These, yes;
phrases.notes: He means these five grains are obligated in חלה.

phrases.english: rice and millet, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limit from the list of grains in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the five grains are obligated in חלה; rice and millet are not.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that only the five grains are obligated in חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for the rule that only these five grains count and rice and millet don't. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule cuts out some foods that look like grain. A limit like that needs a basis in the פסוקים, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these words?': a request for the source of a rule

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that limits חלה to the five grains.

steps.title: Learning חלה from מצה through the word 'bread'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers with a גזרה שוה. The word לחם appears in the חלה verse and in the מצה verse, so חלה applies to the same grains as מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: we learn 'bread' and 'bread' from מצה. Here it says, 'When you eat of the bread of the land,' and there it says, 'bread of affliction.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש links the חלה verse to the מצה verse because both use the word לחם. Whatever grains count for מצה also count for חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזרה שוה, a link between two topics through a shared word. The answer leans on something not yet proven: that מצה can only come from the five grains. The גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It comes from bread, bread': a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה linking two verses that both use the word לֶחֶם
'Bread of the land': the bread that חַלָּה is taken from
'Bread of affliction': a name for מַצָּה

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
It is derived from 'bread' and 'bread' from matza.
It is written here:
'And it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land,'
and it is written there: 'bread of affliction.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה on the word לחם links חלה to מצה, so חלה applies only to grains that are fit for מצה.

steps.title: How do we know which grains count for מצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that מצה itself is limited to the five grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the answer in step 4 rests on a rule about מצה that hasn't been proven yet, so it asks for that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה only copies a rule from one topic to another. If we don't know which grains count for מצה, the link teaches us nothing about חלה. So the base rule needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There itself': the source topic itself, here מַצָּה
'From where do we know it?'

phrases.english: And there itself, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: 'There' means מצה: how do we know מצה must be made from the five grains?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the base rule that step 4 depends on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that מצה can only be made from the five grains.

steps.title: מצה must come from grain that can become חמץ
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, and also the schools of רבי ישמעאל and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, learn from the verse that puts חמץ and מצה side by side. Only grain that can become חמץ can be used for מצה. Rice and millet don't become חמץ; they rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said, and the schools of רבי ישמעאל and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught the same: the verse says, 'Do not eat חמץ with it; for seven days eat מצות with it, bread of affliction.' A person fulfills his obligation on פסח with things that can become חמץ. That leaves out these, which don't become חמץ but only rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three sources that all agree. The verse puts the ban on חמץ right next to the מצוה of מצה. This teaches that מצה must be made from grain that could have become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצה is the same dough as חמץ, just kept from rising. Rice and millet flour mixed with water never rises; it just spoils (סירחון). So it can't be מצה. Through the גזרה שוה from step 4, it isn't obligated in חלה either.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavening: dough rising and becoming חָמֵץ
Rotting or decay, as opposed to rising
Fulfills his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: Only grain that can become חמץ is fit for מצה. Through the word לחם, the same five grains are the only ones obligated in חלה. Rice and millet are left out because they rot instead of rising.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse is not just a ban on חמץ. The proof comes from how close the two halves are: the same grain that could become חמץ is what you use for מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for why only the five grains can be used for מצה on פסח. The same rule decides which grains are obligated in חלה.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said,
and so taught a Sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: and so taught a Sage of the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov:
The verse states: 'You shall not eat leavened bread with it;'

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי״ –
phrases.english: 'seven days you shall eat with it matzot, bread of affliction,'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:3. The proof is that חמץ and מצה sit in the same verse.

phrases.english: with things that can come to leavening,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with them on Passover;

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין בָּאִין לִידֵי חִימּוּץ
phrases.english: this excludes these, which do not come to leavening
phrases.notes: 'These' means rice, millet and similar foods.

phrases.english: but rather to rotting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and completes the source for step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the verse puts חמץ next to מצה, only grain that can become חמץ is fit for מצה. Rice and millet only rot, so they are excluded.

steps.title: Grain, flour and dough join together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the grains join together, and brings a ברייתא: grain, flour and pieces of dough all join with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they join with each other.' It was taught: grain, flours and pieces of dough join with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, that the grains combine (מצטרפין). It brings a ברייתא that extends this to grain at different stages: whole kernels, flour and dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said different grains combine. The ברייתא adds that the same grain at different stages also combines. It doesn't yet say what practical law this is for.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together to reach a minimum amount
Grain (whole kernels)
Flours
Pieces of dough

phrases.english: 'And they join together with each other.'
It was taught:
The grain, the flours, and the pieces of dough
join together with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: combining amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain, flour and dough combine with one another.

steps.title: For what law do they join?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which practical law the ברייתא's joining rule is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this joining actually matters for. It is setting up the answers that come next, in steps 9 and 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Joining' only means something once we know which minimum amount is being reached. The ברייתא didn't say, so the גמרא asks before it can explain the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what law?': asking what practical rule something applies to

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical law the ברייתא in step 7 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law the joining of grain, flour and dough applies to.

steps.title: Three answers: חדש, חמץ on פסח, and מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the joining rule is about חדש. רב יוסף says it is about חמץ בפסח. רב פפא says it is about מעשר שני eaten outside the walls of ירושלים, which brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: it is about new grain. רב יוסף said: it is about חמץ on פסח. רב פפא said: it is about מעשר שני, because if someone eats it outside the wall he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים each answer the question from step 8. Each one names a different eating prohibition where grain, flour and dough would join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three answers are about eating prohibitions. For these you need a minimum amount of food before you are liable. The ברייתא's point would then be that grain, flour and dough pieces add up to that amount together.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain of this year's crop, which may not be eaten before the עומר is brought.
Leavened food, which is forbidden on פסח.
Second tithe. It must be eaten inside ירושלים.
Outside the wall of ירושלים.
He receives lashes.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana says:
It is about the law of new grain.
Rav Yosef says:
It is about the law of leavened food on Pesach.
Rav Pappa says:
It is about the law of second tithe,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אָכֵיל לֵיהּ חוּץ לַחוֹמָה – לָקֵי.
phrases.english: for if one eats it outside the wall, he receives lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with three different suggestions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The joining rule applies to eating prohibitions: חדש, חמץ בפסח, or מעשר שני outside ירושלים.

steps.title: רבא: it is about food becoming impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא is about טומאת אוכלין. It teaches that grain and flour are like dough. Just as dough is plain food, grain and flour join only when they are plain food too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is about the impurity of foods. The ברייתא teaches us that grain and flour are like pieces of dough. Just as dough is food as it is, here too the grain and flour must be food as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a fourth answer. He says the joining rule is about food becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא adds a new detail by comparing grain and flour to dough. Dough is pure food with nothing extra on it. So grain and flour join only when they are plain, edible food without a shell. This sets up the shell discussion that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity of foods. Food needs a minimum size to become impure.
This teaches us (the new point being made).
Pieces of dough.
Food in its plain form, with nothing inedible attached.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not just naming a different law. He is also adding a condition: only plain food joins. The next steps are all about that condition.

phrases.english: Rava says: it is about the impurity of foods,
and this is what it teaches us:
that grain and flours are similar to pieces of dough:
just as there it is food as it is,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the dough, which is pure food with nothing extra on it.

phrases.english: so too here it must be food as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 8's question and adds a condition that only plain food joins.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The joining rule is about food impurity. Grain and flour join like dough, but only when they are plain food.

steps.title: Support: unshelled barley does not join
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that wheat joins whether or not it is shelled. Barley joins only when it is shelled. This supports רבא's condition that only plain food joins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: wheat, whether shelled or not, joins. Barley joins when shelled, and does not join when not shelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבא. It shows that the shell can stop grains from joining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says unshelled barley does not join for impurity. That fits רבא's idea that grain must be plain food to join. For barley, the shell gets in the way.

keyTerms.meaning: Shelled, with the husk removed.
Joins together to make up the minimum amount.
Barley.

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא treats wheat and barley differently. That difference is exactly what the next challenge will question.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: wheat,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קְלוּפָה בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְלוּפָה – מִצְטָרֶפֶת;
phrases.english: whether shelled or not shelled, joins together;
barley, when shelled, joins together;
when not shelled, it does not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: חִטָּה, בֵּין קְלוּפָה בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְלוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רבא's 'plain food' condition.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that only plain food joins for food impurity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: unshelled barley does not join, but shelled barley does.

steps.title: Challenge: seed in its shell counts as normal seed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the barley shell really stops it from counting. The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that 'seed that is sown' means grain the way people sow it, which is wheat, barley and lentils in their shells.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'upon any sowing seed that is sown' means the way people take it out to sow, which is wheat in its shell, barley in its shell, and lentils in their shells.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 11. Another teaching treats barley in its shell as ordinary seed that can become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about seed becoming impure describes seed 'that is sown'. People sow barley in its shell. So the shell seems to count as part of the food, which goes against the idea that unshelled barley does not join.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a challenge opening)
'Sowing seed that is sown', from the verse about seeds and impurity.
In its shell.
Lentils.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Upon any sowing seed that is sown":
in the way that people take it out for sowing:
wheat in its shell, and barley in its shell,
and lentils in their shells.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא brought in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that unshelled barley does not join for food impurity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the verse as covering seed in its sowing form, shell included. That suggests the barley shell counts as part of the food.

steps.title: Moist grain versus dry grain
steps.stepSummary: The two teachings do not argue. One speaks about moist grain and the other about dry grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This teaching is about moist grain, and that teaching is about dry grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 12. One teaching counts barley in its shell, and the other does not, because they are talking about different kinds of grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In moist grain the shell is still part of the kernel, so the school of רבי ישמעאל counts it as seed. In dry grain the shell crumbles and falls away, so it does not count, and barley joins only when it is shelled. This way רבא's rule that only plain food joins still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. Both sources can be true.
Moist (fresh) grain
Dry grain

steps.whatToRemember: Barley shell: when the grain is moist, the shell counts as part of the seed. When it is dry, the shell does not count. This ends the discussion of רבא's joining rule.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
This one is about moist grain; that one is about dry grain.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the teaching from רבי ישמעאל's school, where the shell counts; 'that one' is the barley teaching, where the shell falls off.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּלַחוֹת, הָא בִּיבֵשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings seem to argue about whether a barley shell counts as part of the seed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist barley keeps its shell as part of the seed. Dry barley's shell falls away and does not count.

steps.title: Source for the five-grain rule of חדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the five grains are forbidden as חדש before פסח and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the five grains are forbidden as new crop before פסח. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and starts a new topic. It asks how we know that the law of חדש applies to exactly these five grains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the five grains are forbidden as חדש before the time of פסח. The question is about the scope of the rule: why it applies only to these five grains. This sets up ריש לקיש's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain of this year, forbidden to eat until the עומר is offered
Where do we learn these words from? (a request for the source)

phrases.english: "And they are forbidden as new crop before פסח":
From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It returns to another line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source showing that חדש applies only to the five grains.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'bread' and 'bread' from מצה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the rule through a גזירה שוה. The word 'לחם' (bread) appears both in the law of חדש and in the law of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: we learn it from the word 'bread' here and the word 'bread' for מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the source. The same word 'bread' links חדש to מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word in two places teaches that the two laws work the same way. מצה can only be made from the five grains. So חדש also applies only to the five grains.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from. This is how a גזירה שוה is introduced.
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both places
Bread
Unleavened bread eaten on פסח

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
It is learned from "bread" and "bread" from מצה.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:14 says 'bread' about חדש, and דברים 16:3 says 'bread' about מצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'לחם': just as מצה comes only from the five grains, so does חדש.

steps.title: Source for no reaping before the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the five grains may not be reaped before the עומר and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says it is forbidden to reap the five grains before the עומר. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule in the משנה and asks the same kind of question. It wants to know why the ban on reaping applies to these five grains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked about eating. This question asks about reaping. Again the issue is why the rule is limited to the five grains.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits the new grain
To reap (harvest)

phrases.english: "And to reap before the עומר":
From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as Step 14, now about the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source showing that the ban on reaping before the עומר applies only to the five grains.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'first' and 'first' from חלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns the rule through a גזירה שוה. The word 'ראשית' (first) appears both in the law of the עומר and in the law of חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: we learn it from the word 'first' here and the word 'first' for חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source. The same word 'first' links the עומר harvest to חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה is taken only from dough made of the five grains. Since the same word appears in both places, the ban on reaping before the עומר also covers only the five grains.

keyTerms.meaning: First (the first part)
The portion of dough given to the כהן

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
It is learned from "first" and "first" from חלה.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:10 says 'first' about the עומר, and במדבר 15:20 says 'first' about חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'ראשית': just as חלה applies only to the five grains, so does the ban on reaping before the עומר.

steps.title: What does 'before the עומר' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point in time the משנה means by 'before the עומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'before the עומר' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of a phrase in the משנה. This sets up the two opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is first reaped and later brought as an offering. The question is which of these two events is the cutoff point.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the עומר

phrases.english: What is meant by "before the עומר"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the time phrase in the rule whose source was just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'before the עומר' means before its reaping or before its offering.

steps.title: רבי יונה: before the reaping of the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה says the cutoff is the reaping of the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said: it means before the עומר is reaped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונה gives the first answer. The time limit ends once the עומר is cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the key event is the cutting of the עומר grain. Once that happens, the restriction ends, even before the offering is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The reaping (cutting) of the עומר grain

phrases.english: רבי יונה says:
Before the reaping of the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cutoff is the reaping of the עומר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר זבדא: before the bringing of the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר זבדא says the cutoff is when the עומר is brought as an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר זבדא said: it means before the עומר is brought.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר זבדא disagrees with רבי יונה. The time limit lasts until the עומר is actually offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering comes later than the reaping. So by this view the restriction lasts longer: reaping the עומר is not enough, and the restriction ends only with the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The bringing (offering) of the עומר

steps.whatToRemember: 'Before the עומר' has two readings. רבי יונה says before it is reaped. רבי יוסי בר זבדא says before it is offered.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי בר זבדא says:
Before the bringing of the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposing answer to Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cutoff is the bringing of the עומר offering.

steps.title: The משנה's wording fits the view that the cutoff is bringing the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which lists the ban on eating חדש and the ban on reaping as two separate clauses. That fits the view that חדש stays forbidden until the עומר is brought, because then eating and reaping become allowed at different times.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the grains are forbidden as new grain before פסח, and forbidden to reap before the עומר. This makes sense for the one who said the cutoff is the bringing of the עומר. That is why the משנה did not combine the two and teach them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and points out that it lists two separate time limits. This is a setup: the גמרא is about to use it to challenge the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses two different time markers: 'before פסח' for eating and 'before the עומר' for reaping. Under the 'bringing' view, reaping becomes allowed once the עומר is reaped, but eating חדש stays forbidden until the עומר offering is brought later that day. The two bans end at different moments, so the separate clauses make sense under this view.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain of this year's crop, forbidden to eat until the עומר
'It makes sense…', opening a contrast: one view fits, but the other is hard
The bringing (offering) of the עומר
Combines, mixes together

phrases.english: We learned: they are forbidden as new grain before פסח,
and to reap them before the עומר.
It makes sense according to the one who said
'before the bringing of the עומר'

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּלָא קָא עָרֵיב לְהוּ וְתָנֵי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: that is why it does not combine them and teach them together.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹדֶם הֲבָאַת הָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the argument from steps 19-20 against the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the cutoff is the reaping of the עומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup half: the separate clauses fit the 'bringing' view, which prepares the contrast in the next step.

steps.title: Under the reaping view, the משנה should have combined the clauses
steps.stepSummary: If new grain becomes allowed once the עומר is reaped, eating and reaping end at the same time, so the משנה should have written one combined phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who said the cutoff is the reaping of the עומר, let the משנה combine them and teach: they are forbidden as new grain and to reap before פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that the cutoff is the reaping of the עומר. Under that view the משנה's wording looks wasteful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both eating and reaping become allowed at the same moment, there was no reason to split them into two clauses with two different time markers. The משנה could have said it all in one line. Since it did not, the reaping view seems to clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The reaping (cutting) of the עומר grain
Let it combine them
And teach them (together)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹדֶם קְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: But according to the one who said 'before the reaping of the עומר',
let it combine them and teach them:
'They are forbidden as new grain and to reap before פסח!'
phrases.notes: This is the shorter wording the גמרא says the משנה could have used, with one time marker for both bans.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹדֶם קְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר לִיעָרְבִינְהוּ וְלִיתְנִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא contrast begun in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that 'before the עומר' means before its reaping
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both bans end together, the משנה's separate clauses are unnecessary. That suggests the reaping view does not match the משנה.

steps.title: The argument was really about the משנה's later clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the argument: it was not about the reaping clause but about the later line, 'if they took root before the עומר, the עומר permits them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if the argument was stated, it was stated about the later clause: 'If they took root before the עומר, the עומר permits them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the argument was never about the reaping clause. It applies the argument to a different line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now everyone agrees about the reaping clause, so the challenge from the משנה's wording falls away. The open question is a different one: grain must take root before 'the עומר' for that עומר to permit it, and the גמרא now asks which moment counts.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was stated, used to move an argument to a different place
On the later clause (סיפא) of the משנה
They took root
Permits them

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
it was stated on the later clause:
'If they took root before the עומר,
the עומר permits them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 22 by moving the argument to another clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the argument was about the reaping clause, which made the reaping view clash with the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about the clause on grain that took root before the עומר, so the wording of the reaping clause poses no problem.

steps.title: What does 'before the עומר' mean in the later clause?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which moment 'before the עומר' refers to in the clause about taking root.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'before the עומר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what moment counts as 'before the עומר' for grain that took root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as step 18, but now it is asked about the taking-root clause. The answer decides which grain the coming עומר permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the עומר

phrases.english: What is 'before the עומר'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the question of step 18 for the clause chosen in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'before the עומר' in the taking-root clause means before its bringing or before its reaping.

steps.title: The two opinions restated, with the names switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה says it means before the bringing of the עומר; רבי יוסי בר זבדא says before the reaping of the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה says: before the bringing of the עומר. רבי יוסי בר זבדא says: before the reaping of the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the two opinions again, now applied to the taking-root clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the opinions appear the other way around from steps 19-20. Now רבי יונה holds 'bringing' and רבי יוסי בר זבדא holds 'reaping'. Under the reaping view, grain that took root after the עומר was reaped but before it was offered would not be permitted by this עומר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names! In steps 19-20 רבי יונה said 'reaping' and רבי יוסי בר זבדא said 'bringing'. In this restated version it is the other way around.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's wording shows that the argument is not about when reaping becomes allowed. It is about which grain counts as having taken root 'before the עומר'.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר: קוֹדֶם הֲבָאַת הָעוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: רבי יונה says: before the bringing of the עומר,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זַבְדָּא אוֹמֵר: קוֹדֶם קְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי בר זבדא says: before the reaping of the עומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר קוֹדֶם הֲבָאַת הָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יונה: before the bringing; רבי יוסי בר זבדא: before the reaping.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins to respond

steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here, so the actual argument comes in the next section. It follows directly on the restated argument in step 25.
